nodes.name: Sub-Gaussian weights $\xi_{ij}$
nodes.statement:
Let $\{\xi_{ij}\}_{i=1,\ldots,N_1\,,j=1,\ldots,N_2}$ a doubly indexed sequence of i.i.d. centred sub-Gaussian r.vs. with 
$$
E[\xi_{ij}\xi_{hk}]=\delta_{ih}\delta_{jk}\,, 
$$
nodes.statement_short: The weights are an i.i.d. array of centred sub-Gaussian random variables with unit variance.

nodes.name: Proportional layer sizes
nodes.statement:
For definiteness we  assume that
$$
\frac{N_1}{N_1+N_2}\to \alpha\in(0,1)\,.
$$

nodes.name: Random matrix $\Xi$ and sample covariance matrix
nodes.statement: We shall look at this sequence in two different ways, namely as entries of a $N_1\times N_2$ random matrix $\Xi$ or a collection of $N_2$ patterns in $\mathbb{R}^{N_1}$, defining a sample covariance matrix  $\frac{1}{N_2}\Xi\Xi^T\in\mathbb{R}^{N_1\times N_1}$.
nodes.statement_short: The weights form an $N_1\times N_2$ matrix $\Xi$ with sample covariance $\Xi\Xi^T/N_2$.

nodes.name: Eigenvalue and singular value notation
nodes.statement: For $A\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times N}$ we denote its eigenvalues as $\lambda_i:=\lambda_{i}(A)$, $i=1,\ldots N$; for $A\in\mathbb{R}^{N_1\times N_2}$ we denote its singular values as $\sigma_i:=\sigma_{i}(A)$, $i=1,\ldots N_1$.

nodes.name: Marchenko-Pastur law (P1)
nodes.statement:
The empirical distribution of the eigenvalues of $\frac{1}{N_2}\Xi\Xi^T$ converges a.s. to the Marchenko-Pastur law:
$$
\frac{1}{N_1}\sum_{j=1}^{N_1}\delta(\lambda-\lambda_i(\frac{1}{N_2}\Xi\Xi^T)) \rightharpoonup \rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)\quad \mathbb P-a.s.
$$
where
\begin{equation} \rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha):= (2-\frac{1}{\alpha})^+\delta_0(\lambda) +\frac{(1-\alpha)}{2\pi \alpha}\frac{\sqrt{(\lambda-\lambda_-)(\lambda_+-\lambda)}}{\lambda}1_{[\lambda_-,\lambda_+]}(\lambda)
\end{equation}
with  $\lambda_{\pm}:=\left(1\pm\sqrt{\alpha/(1-\alpha)}\right)^2$.
conclusions: The empirical distribution of the eigenvalues of $\frac{1}{N_2}\Xi\Xi^T$ converges a.s. to the Marchenko-Pastur law
nodes.statement_short: The empirical spectral distribution of the sample covariance converges a.s. to the Marchenko-Pastur law $\rho_{MP}(\cdot;\alpha)$.

nodes.name: Marchenko-Pastur density
nodes.statement: \rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha):= (2-\frac{1}{\alpha})^+\delta_0(\lambda) +\frac{(1-\alpha)}{2\pi \alpha}\frac{\sqrt{(\lambda-\lambda_-)(\lambda_+-\lambda)}}{\lambda}1_{[\lambda_-,\lambda_+]}(\lambda)
nodes.label: eq:MP

nodes.name: Spectrum localisation (P2)
conclusions: The spectrum of $\frac{1}{N_2}\Xi\Xi^T$ is localised in an interval with large probability
nodes.statement_short: The operator norm of $\Xi\Xi^T/N_2-\mathbb I$ exceeds $\sqrt{\lambda_+}-1+t$ with probability at most $2e^{-N_1t^2/2}$.

nodes.name: Operator-norm tail bound
nodes.statement: \mathbb P(\|\frac {1}{N_2}\Xi\Xi^T-\mathbb I\|_{op}\geq t+\sqrt{\lambda_+}-1)\leq 2e^{-\frac {N_1t^2}{2}}\,.
nodes.label: eq:impo-spectrum

nodes.name: Sphere $S^N(R)$
nodes.statement: Let $S^{N}(R)$ be the $(N-1)$-dimensional sphere in $\mathbb{R}^N$ with radius $R\sqrt N$.

nodes.name: Spherical and Gaussian priors
nodes.label: eq:prior

nodes.name: Regularising function $r$ (one layer)
nodes.statement:
Let  $r\,:\mathbb{R}\mapsto\mathbb{R}$ such that there is $\varepsilon>0$ with
$$
\lim_{x\to\infty}\frac{r(x)}{x^{2+\varepsilon}}=\infty\,.
$$
nodes.statement_short: A regularising function $r$ growing faster than $x^{2+\varepsilon}$ at infinity.

nodes.name: Regularised prior $\rho_N$
nodes.statement: \rho_N(dx):= e^{-Nr\left(\frac{\|x\|}{\sqrt N}\right)}\gamma_{N,\theta}(dx)\,.
nodes.label: eq:Reg-prior1

nodes.name: Regularising function $r$ (two layers)
nodes.statement:
We introduce some $r\,:\,\mathbb{R}^2\mapsto \mathbb{R}$ so that
$$
\lim_{x^2+y^2\to\infty} \frac{r(x,y)}{x^2}=\lim_{x^2+y^2\to\infty} \frac{r(x,y)}{y^2}=\infty\,.
$$
nodes.statement_short: A two-variable regularising function $r(x,y)$ growing superquadratically in each variable.

nodes.name: Two-layer regularised prior $\rho^2$
nodes.statement: \rho^2_{N_1,N_2}(dxdy):= e^{-\sqrt{N_1N_2}r\left(\frac{\|x\|}{\sqrt N_1},\frac{\|y\|}{\sqrt N_2}\right)}\gamma_{N_1,\theta}(dx)\gamma_{N_2,\theta}(dy)\,.
nodes.label: eq:Reg-prior2

nodes.name: Spherical shell
nodes.statement: S_{N,R,\varepsilon}:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^N\,:\,R-\varepsilon\leq\|x\|_2\leq R+\varepsilon\}\,.
nodes.label: eq:Sfshell

nodes.name: Uniform probability on a spherical shell
nodes.statement:
We denote (here and further $|A|$ is the Lebesgue measure of the set $A$)
$$
\sigma_{N,R.\varepsilon}(dx):=|S_{\varepsilon,N,R}|^{-1}1_{\{S_{\varepsilon,N,R}\}}(x)dx\,
$$
the uniform probability on a shell and note that it is a.c. w.r.t. $\gamma_{N,\theta}$.
nodes.genus: the uniform probability on a shell

nodes.name: Shell volume relation
nodes.statement: |S_{\varepsilon,N,R}|=\varepsilon|S_{N,R}|+\OOO{\varepsilon^2}\,.
nodes.label: eq:shells-surface

nodes.name: Generic prior notation $\mu$, $\mu^2$
nodes.statement: Let $\mu_{(\cdot)}\in\{\sigma_{(\cdot)},\gamma_{(\cdot)},\rho_{(\cdot)}\}$ and $\mu^2_{(\cdot)}\in\{\sigma_{(\cdot)},\gamma_{(\cdot)}\}\otimes \{\sigma_{(\cdot)},\gamma_{(\cdot)}\}\cup\{\rho_{(\cdot)}^2\}$ denote one prior among the one introduced before respectively for the one-layer and the bipartite machine.

nodes.name: Gibbs measures of HM and RBM
nodes.label: eq:Gibbs

nodes.name: Partition function
nodes.statement: The normalisation $Z_{N_1,N_2,\beta}$ is called partition function and it needs not to be the same, despite the symbol.

nodes.name: Free energies of HM and RBM
nodes.statement: A^{HM}_{N_1,N_2}(\beta):=\frac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log Z_{N_1,N_2,\beta}\qquad A^{RBM}_{N_1,N_2}(\beta):=\frac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log Z_{N_1,N_2,\beta}\,.
nodes.label: eq:free

nodes.name: Thermodynamic limit
nodes.statement:
Most interesting is to evaluate the last quantities in the so-called thermodynamic limit, namely
$$
N_1,N_2\to\infty\,,\quad\mbox{such that }\qquad \lim_{N_1,N_2}\frac{N_1}{N_1+N_2}=:\alpha>0\,.
$$

nodes.name: High-load regime
nodes.statement: The regime $\alpha\neq0,1$ is called high-load and we will stick to that in this work.

nodes.name: Self-averaging of the free energy
nodes.statement: Being Lipschitz functions of the weights, free energies always satisfies a concentration inequality which ensures their a.s. convergence to the expected value.
assumptions: Being Lipschitz functions of the weights
conclusions: free energies always satisfies a concentration inequality which ensures their a.s. convergence to the expected value

nodes.name: Equal layer parameters
nodes.statement: For simplicity we will assume always the distributions of the two layers to have the same parameters, \textit{i.e. } radius and variance.

nodes.name: Free energy notation $A_\mu(X,\alpha,\beta)$
nodes.statement: In general $A_\mu(X,\alpha,\beta)$ denotes the free energy of a BM with prior $\mu$ whose parameters are $X$.

nodes.name: Hat notation for spherical shell priors
nodes.statement: Only exception, the quantities of interest referred to spherical shell priors are indicated by $\widehat \cdot$ for all the models.

nodes.name: Scheme of equivalences between Boltzmann machines
nodes.section: Main result and organisation of the paper
nodes.statement_short: Diagram of the marginalisation and Legendre-transform equivalences among $HM_\sigma$, $HM_\rho$, $RBM_{\sigma\gamma}$, $RBM_{\sigma\sigma}$, $RBM_{\rho\gamma}$, $RBM_{\rho^2}$, with their validity in high or low load.

nodes.name: Marginalisation equivalence of RBM and Hopfield model
nodes.statement:
Marginalisation is the usual trick of RBMs. The two layers are coupled linearly, so that one can integrate out \'a la Stratonovich the units from the Gaussian layer in the partition function of a RBM to obtain the partition function of a HM (with $\beta^2$ replacing $\beta$). 
All the relevant quantities (e.g. Gibbs measures, free energy, order parameters etc) of one model can be computed directly from the one of the other one. For instance the equivalence $HM_\sigma\leftrightarrow RBM_{\sigma,\gamma}$ at the level of Gibbs measure reads as
$$
Z^{-1}_{N_1,N_2,\beta}\sigma_{N_2,R}(dx)\int_{\mathbb{R}^{N_2}}\gamma_{N_2,\theta}(dy)e^{\beta H_{N_1,N_2}^{RBM}}=Z^{-1}_{N_1,N_2,\beta}\sigma_{N_1,R}(dx)e^{\frac{\beta^2}{\theta^2} H^{HM}_{N_1}}\,,
$$
since the  partition functions of the two models are numerically the same.
nodes.section: Main result and organisation of the paper
assumptions: The two layers are coupled linearly
conclusions: one can integrate out \'a la Stratonovich the units from the Gaussian layer in the partition function of a RBM to obtain the partition function of a HM (with $\beta^2$ replacing $\beta$)
nodes.statement_short: Integrating out the Gaussian layer of an RBM (Hubbard-Stratonovich) gives the Hopfield partition function at $\beta^2$.

nodes.section: Main result and organisation of the paper

nodes.section: Main result and organisation of the paper
assumptions: let $\rho_N, \rho^2_N$ be defined as in (\ref{eq:Reg-prior1}), (\ref{eq:Reg-prior2}) and discussion around
nodes.statement_short: The free energies of spherical and (regularised) Gaussian HM and RBM are Legendre transforms of each other, with squared radius and inverse variance conjugate.

nodes.name: HM Legendre formula
nodes.statement: A_\rho(\theta,\alpha,\beta)=\alpha \sup_{R>0}\left( \alpha^{-1}A_{\sigma}(R,\beta) -\frac{R^2}{2\theta}+\log R- r(R) -\frac12(\log\theta-1) \right)\,;

nodes.statement: A_{\sigma}(R,\beta)=\alpha \inf_{\theta>0}\left(\frac{R^2}{2\theta}+\alpha^{-1}A_\rho(\theta,\alpha,\beta) -\log R+ r(R)+\frac12(\log\theta-1)\right)\,.

nodes.statement: A_{\sigma,\gamma}(\theta,R_2,\alpha,\beta)=\alpha\sup_{R_1>0}\left(\alpha^{-1}A_{\sigma\sigma}(R_1,R_2,\beta)-\frac{R_1^2}{2\theta}+\log R_1 -\frac12(\log\theta-1)\right)\,;

nodes.name: Free energy of the spherical Hopfield model
assumptions: Let $A_{N_1,N_2}$ denote the free energy of $HM_{\sigma}$.
nodes.statement_short: The limiting free energy of $HM_\sigma$ is a one-parameter convex minimum over $q$ of a Marchenko-Pastur log-integral.
nodes.label: Th:HM-sfer

nodes.name: Spherical HM free energy formula
nodes.statement: \lim_{N_1,N_2\to\infty} A_{N_1,N_2} = \alpha\min_{2q\geq \beta(1-\alpha)\lambda_+}\left(q R^2 -\frac 12\int\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)\log(2q-\beta(1-\alpha)\lambda) d\lambda-\log R-\frac12\right)\,.

nodes.name: Free energy of the doubly spherical RBM
assumptions: Let $A_{N_1,N_2}$ denote the free energy of $RBM_{\sigma\sigma}$ and $\alpha\leq \frac 12$.
nodes.statement_short: For $\alpha\le 1/2$ the limiting free energy of $RBM_{\sigma\sigma}$ is a jointly convex minimum over $(a,b)$ with $ab\ge\beta^2(1-\alpha)\lambda_+$.
nodes.label: Th:Bip-sfer

nodes.name: Doubly spherical RBM free energy formula
nodes.statement:
\lim_{N_1,N_2\to\infty} A_{N_1,N_2} &=&\min_{ab\geq \beta^2(1-\alpha)\lambda_+}\left(\frac{R^2}{2}\left(\alpha a + (1-\alpha) b\right) -\frac 1 2 (1-2\alpha)\log(b)\right. \nonumber \\
 &-&\left.\frac \alpha2\int\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)\log(ab-\beta^2(1-\alpha)\lambda) d\lambda-\log R-\frac12\right) \,.

nodes.name: Choice $\alpha\leq 1/2$
nodes.statement: The choice $\alpha\leq\frac12$ is just a matter of convenience as it will be clear that pre-choosing the largest layer simplifies a lot the notations. For $\alpha\geq \frac12$ one should bear in mind that the Marchenko-Pastur distribution (\ref{eq:MP}) has an atom in zero.

nodes.name: Spherical shell approximation
nodes.statement:
Let $\widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}$ denote the free energy of $HM_{\sigma_\varepsilon}$, $RBM_{\sigma_\varepsilon\sigma}$ or $RBM_{\sigma_\varepsilon\sigma_\varepsilon}$. Then it is
$$
\lim_{\varepsilon\to0}\lim_{N_1,N_2} \widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}=\lim_{N_1,N_2}\lim_{\varepsilon\to0} \widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}\,. 
$$
assumptions: Let $\widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}$ denote the free energy of $HM_{\sigma_\varepsilon}$, $RBM_{\sigma_\varepsilon\sigma}$ or $RBM_{\sigma_\varepsilon\sigma_\varepsilon}$.
nodes.statement_short: The limits $\varepsilon\to0$ (shell thickness) and $N\to\infty$ commute for the shell-prior free energies.
nodes.label: lemma-gusci

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.3
nodes.statement:
In this proof we write $N$ to mean $N_1$ or $N_2$ and by $A^{\sigma}(R; \beta)$ the free energy of a spherical model of radius $R$, according to the context. No further details are needed. By Fubini and the mean value theorem there is a $R^*_\varepsilon\in[R\sqrt N-\varepsilon,R\sqrt N+\varepsilon]$ for which
$$
\widehat A_{N_1,N_2}=A_{N_1,N_2}^{\sigma}(R^*_\varepsilon; \beta)\,. 
$$
By a simple change of variables we have
$$
A_{N_1,N_2}^{\sigma}(R^*_\varepsilon; \beta)=A_{N_1,N_2}^{\sigma}(R; c_{N,\varepsilon}\beta)\,, 
$$
with $c_{N,\varepsilon}:=R^2_\varepsilon/R^2N$. Therefore by Lipschitz continuity of the free energy w.r.t. $\beta$
$$
|A^\sigma_{N_1,N_2}-\widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}|\leq \frac\varepsilon N\,. 
$$
This, combined with $A^\sigma_{N_1,N_2}=\lim_{\varepsilon\to0} \widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}$, gives the assert.
nodes.statement_short: Mean value theorem picks a radius in the shell; rescaling the radius into $\beta$ and Lipschitz continuity in $\beta$ give an $\varepsilon/N$ bound.

nodes.name: Diagonalisation of the spherical Hopfield energy
nodes.statement:
The best advantage of the spherical prior is that one can diagonalise the energy (\ref{eq:HM}):
$$
H(x)=-(1-\alpha)\sum_{i=1}^{N_1}\lambda_ix_i^2\,.
$$

nodes.statement_short: Disorder realisations with operator norm above $a>\lambda_+$ contribute $O(e^{-cN_1})$ to the expected free energy.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.1
nodes.statement:
Let $2q>\beta(1-\alpha)\lambda_+$. Then using (\ref{eq:shells-surface}) we have 
\begin{eqnarray}
\varepsilon \hat{Z}_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}(\beta,\alpha,R)&=& \varepsilon\ e^{q R^2 N_1}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{N_1}}\sigma_{N_1,R,\varepsilon}(dz)e^{-\sum_i^{N_1}(q-\frac{\beta(1-\alpha)}{2}\lambda_i)z_i^2} \\
&\leq&e^{q R^2 N_1}\frac{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}2}}{|S_{R\sqrt{N_1}}|}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}\frac{dz}{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}2}} e^{-\sum_i^{N_1}(2q-\beta(1-\alpha)\lambda_i)z_i^2/2}\nonumber\\
&=&e^{q R^2 N_1}\frac{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}2}}{|S_{R\sqrt{N}}|}e^{-\frac 12\sum_i^N\log(2q-\beta(1-\alpha)\lambda_i)}\nonumber\,,
\end{eqnarray}
therefore, since $\frac 1{N_1} \log \left(|S_{R\sqrt{N_1}}| /\sqrt{2\pi}^{N_1}  \right) \to \log R +\frac 1 2$ and thanks to Lemma \ref{lemma-gusci} 
$$
\lim\sup_{N_1,N_2}\frac1{N_1+N_2} \log Z_{N_1,N_2}(\beta,\alpha,R)\leq \alpha q R^2 -\frac \alpha2\int\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)\log(2q-\beta(1-\alpha)\lambda)-\alpha\log R-\frac\alpha2=:\tilde A(q)\,,
$$
whence, as $\tilde A(q)$ is continuous, 
$$
\lim\sup_{N_1,N_2}\frac{1}{N_1+N_2} \log Z_{N_1,N_2}(\beta,\alpha,R)\leq\min_{2q\geq\beta(1-\alpha)\lambda_+}\tilde A(q).
$$ 
Moreover for $2q>\beta(1-\alpha)\lambda_+$
$$
\partial_q^2 \tilde A(q)=2\alpha\int d\lambda\frac{\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)}{(2q-\beta(1-\alpha)\lambda)^2}>0,
$$
thus $\tilde A(q)$ is  convex and the minimum is attained in a unique point $\bar q$. 
 
\noindent Now the reverse bound. Let $\varepsilon>0$ and $S^c_{N_1,R,\varepsilon}$ the complementary set of the shell $S_{N_1,R,\varepsilon}$. It holds
$$
\varepsilon \widehat Z_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}=e^{ q R^2 N_1}\frac{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}{2}}}{|S_{R\sqrt{N_1}}|}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{N_1}}\frac{dz}{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}{2}}} e^{-\sum_i^{N_1}(q-\frac{\beta(1-\alpha)}{2}\lambda_i)z_i^2}-e^{ q R^2 N_1}\frac{(2\pi)^{\frac N2}}{|S_{R\sqrt{N_1}}|}\int_{S_{N_1,R,\varepsilon}^c}\frac{dz}{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}2}} e^{-\sum_i^{N_1}(q-\frac{\beta(1-\alpha)}{2}\lambda_i)z_i^2}.
$$
For any $\eta>0$ small enough we have
\begin{eqnarray}
\int_{S_{N_1,R,\varepsilon}^c}\frac{dz}{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}2}} e^{-\sum_i^{N_1}(q-\frac{\beta(1-\alpha)}{2}\lambda_i)z_i^2}&\leq&\exp\left[N_1\left(\eta\left(R^2-\frac\varepsilon {N_1}\right)-\frac{1}{2N_1}\sum_j\log(2q-\beta\lambda_j+2\eta)\right)\right]\nonumber\\
&+&\exp\left[N_1\left(-\eta\left(R^2+\frac\varepsilon {N_1}\right)-\frac{1}{2N_1}\sum_j\log(2q-\beta\lambda_j-2\eta)\right)\right]\nonumber.
\end{eqnarray}
\noindent Note now that the r.h.s. is $o(e^{-N})$ if $\frac\varepsilon N\to\infty$ as $N\to\infty$. So the greatest contribution is at the scale $\varepsilon=\tilde\varepsilon N$, $\tilde\varepsilon>0$ independent on $N_1$. Therefore
\begin{equation} \lim\inf_{N_1,N_2}\widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\tilde\varepsilon}\geq\max\left(\tilde A(q), A^1_{\tilde\varepsilon}(\eta; q), A^2_{\tilde\varepsilon}(\eta; q)\right),
\end{equation}
with
\begin{eqnarray}
A^1_{\tilde\varepsilon}(\eta; q)&=&\alpha(q+\eta)R^2-\alpha\tilde\varepsilon\eta-\frac\alpha2\int d\lambda\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)\log(2(q+\eta)-\beta\lambda)-\alpha\log R-\frac\alpha2;\\
A^2_{\tilde\varepsilon}(\eta; q)&=&\alpha(q-\eta)R^2-\alpha\tilde\varepsilon\eta-\frac\alpha2\int d\lambda\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)\log(2(q-\eta)-\beta\lambda)-\alpha\log R-\frac\alpha2.
\end{eqnarray}
Now we show that if $\bar q$ is the unique minimiser of $\tilde A(q)$ it is for $\eta$ small enough
$$
\tilde A(\bar q)=\max\left(\tilde A(\bar q), A^1_{\tilde\varepsilon}(\eta; \bar q), A^2_{\tilde\varepsilon}(\eta; \bar q)\right)\,,
$$
which will conclude the proof.

To do so we introduce
\begin{eqnarray}
\Delta_-(q;\eta)&:=&\tilde A(q)-A^1_{\tilde\varepsilon}(\eta; q)= -\alpha\eta(R^2-\tilde\varepsilon)+\frac\alpha2\int d\lambda\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)\log\left(\frac{2(q+\eta)-\beta\lambda}{2q-\beta\lambda}\right);\\
\Delta_+(q;\eta)&:=&\tilde A(q)-A^2_{\tilde\varepsilon}(\eta; q)= \alpha\eta(R^2+\tilde\varepsilon)+\frac\alpha2\int d\lambda\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)\log\left(\frac{2(q-\eta)-\beta\lambda}{2q-\beta\lambda}\right)\,.
\end{eqnarray}
\noindent As a function of $\eta$, $\Delta_\pm(q;\eta)$ are continuous and differentiable, vanishing in $\eta=0$ and with $\lim_{\eta\to+\infty}\Delta_\pm(q,\eta)=\pm\infty$. Moreover $\Delta_+(q;\eta)$ is uniformly convex and $\Delta_-(q;\eta)$ uniformly concave. Thus $\Delta_-(q;\eta)$ assumes a positive maximum iff the derivative in $\eta=0$ is positive, that is
\begin{equation} 0<-(R^2-\tilde\varepsilon)+\int d\lambda\frac{\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)}{2q-\beta\lambda}=\tilde \varepsilon-\partial_q \tilde A(q)\,.
\end{equation}

\noindent Likewise for $\Delta_+(q;\eta)$ is always positive iff 
$\left.\partial_\eta \Delta_+(q;\eta)\right|_{\eta=0}\geq0$, \textit{i.e. }
\begin{equation} 0\leq(R^2+\tilde\varepsilon)+\int d\lambda\frac{\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)}{2q-\beta\lambda}=\tilde \varepsilon+\partial_q \tilde A(q).
\end{equation}
Combining (\ref{eq:upper-bound-epsi1}) and (\ref{eq:upper-bound-epsi2}) we get
$$
-\tilde\varepsilon\leq \left.\partial_q \tilde A(q)\right|_{q=\tilde q}<\tilde\varepsilon\,,,
$$
that is $\tilde q$ is the unique stationary point of $\tilde A(q)$. With this choice of $q$, relation (\ref{eq:max( , , )}) gives
\begin{equation}
\lim\inf_{N_1,N_2} \widehat A_{N_1,N_2.\tilde \varepsilon}\geq \min_{q\geq\beta\lambda_+}\tilde A(q) \,.
\end{equation}
As $\tilde\varepsilon$ can be taken arbitrarily small, we recover (\ref{eq:AHMsfer}).

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.2
nodes.statement:
Now  start from (\ref{eq:diagRBM}) and write for any $a,b$ such that $ab>\beta^2(1-\alpha)\lambda_+$
\begin{eqnarray}
Z_{N_1,N_2}&=&\int\sigma_1(dx)\sigma_2(dy) \exp\left( \sqrt{1-\alpha} \beta\sum_{i\in[N_1]}x_iy_i\sigma_i-\frac a2 \|x\|^2-\frac b2 \|y\|^2+\frac a2 R^2N_1+\frac b2 R^2N_2\right)\nonumber\\
&=&\exp\left(\frac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)\right) \int\sigma_1(dx)\sigma_2(dy)\exp\left( -\frac 1 2 \sum_{i=1}^{N_2} (z_i^T,M_i z_i)\right) \,,
\end{eqnarray}
where we have defined 
$$
z^T_i := \begin{cases}
(x_i,y_i)&i=1,\ldots , N_1\,,\\
(0,y_i)&i=N_1+1,\ldots , N_2
\end{cases}$$
and the $2\times 2$ symmetric positively defined matrix 
$$
M_i :=
  \left( {\begin{array}{cc}
   a & -\beta\sqrt{1-\alpha}\sigma_i \\
   -\beta\sqrt{1-\alpha}\sigma_i & b \\
\end{array} } \right)\,,\quad i\in[N_1]\qquad M_i:=\mathrm{diag}(0,b)\,,\quad i=N_1+1,\ldots , N_2\,.
$$ 
Thus by (\ref{eq:shells-surface})
\begin{eqnarray}
\varepsilon^2\hat{Z}_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}&\leq& \exp\left(\frac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)\right) \frac{(2\pi)^{\frac{N_1}{2}} (2\pi)^{\frac{N_2}{2}} }{S^R_{N_1} S^R_{N_2}} \int \frac{dx dy}{\sqrt{2\pi}^N}\exp\left( -\frac 12\sum_{i=1}^{N_2} (z_i^T,M_i z_i)\right),\nonumber\\ 

&=& \exp\left(\frac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)\right) \frac{(2\pi)^{\frac{N_1}{2}} (2\pi)^{\frac{N_2}{2}} }{S^R_{N_1} S^R_{N_2}} b^{-\frac{N_2-N_1}{2}} \prod_{i=1}^{N_1}(ab-\beta^2(1-\alpha)\sigma^2_i)^{-\frac 12}\,.
\end{eqnarray}

We introduce
\begin{equation} \bar A(a,b):= \frac {R^2}{2} (a\alpha+b(1-\alpha))-\log R-\frac12-\frac{1-2\alpha}{2}\log b -\frac{\alpha}{2}\int \rho_{MP}(d\lambda;\alpha)\log(ab-(1-\alpha)\beta^2\lambda)\,.
\end{equation}
and 
$$
\lim\sup_{N_1,N_2}A_{N_1,N_2}\leq \bar A(a,b)\,,\quad \forall a,b>0\,:\,\,ab>(1-\alpha)\beta^2\lambda_+\,. 
$$
A direct inspection shows that $A(a,b)$ is jointly uniformly convex for any $\alpha\in[0,1/2]$ if $ab>(1-\alpha)\beta^2\lambda_+$, therefore
\begin{equation} \lim\sup_{N_1,N_2}A_{N_1,N_2}\leq \min_{ab>(1-\alpha)\beta^2\lambda_+} \bar A(a,b)\,. 
\end{equation}

We record for later use the gradient coordinates 
\begin{eqnarray}
\partial_a \bar A(a,b)&=&\frac{\alpha R^2}{2}-\frac\alpha2\int \rho_{MP}(d\lambda;\alpha)\frac{b}{ab- (1-\alpha)\beta^2\lambda}\,; \\
\partial_b \bar A(a,b)&=&\frac{(1-\alpha)R^2}{2} -\frac{1-2\alpha}{2b}-\frac\alpha2\int \rho_{MP}(d\lambda;\alpha)\frac{a}{ab- (1-\alpha)\beta^2\lambda}\,. \end{eqnarray}













For the reverse bound consider again  spherical shells around $S_{R,N_1}$ and $S_{R,N_2}$ of thickness $\varepsilon$, that we name respectively $S_{1,\varepsilon}$ and $S_{2,\varepsilon}$. We split $S_{1,\varepsilon}=\mathbb{R}^{N_1}\setminus S^c_{1,\varepsilon}$ and $S_{2,\varepsilon}=\mathbb{R}^{N_2}\setminus S^c_{2,\varepsilon}$ and set $S_{\varepsilon}:=S_{1,\varepsilon}\times S_{2,\varepsilon}$. We have

\begin{eqnarray}
\varepsilon^2 \widehat Z_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}&:=&\varepsilon^2\int\sigma_{N_1, R,\varepsilon}(dx)\sigma_{N_2,R,\varepsilon}(dy)e^{-\beta H_N(x,y)}\nonumber\\
&=&\exp\left(\frac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)\right) \int_{\mathbb{R}^{N_1}\times \mathbb{R}^{N_2}} \frac{dxdy}{|S_1||S_2|}\exp\left( -\frac 1 2 \sum_{i=1}^{N_2} (z_i^T,M_i z_i)\right)\nonumber\\
&-&\exp\left(\frac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)\right) \int_{S^c_{\varepsilon}} \frac{dxdy}{|S_1||S_2|}\exp\left( -\frac 1 2 \sum_{i=1}^{N_2} (z_i^T,M_i z_i)\right) \,,
\end{eqnarray}
where we used again the representation (\ref{eq:repr-Z-RBM}). The free energy associated to the first summand was already computed above in the thermodynamic limit. Therefore we have to upper bound the second summand. We consider four contributions according to the following decomposition. Let $\kappa\in\{-1,1\}$ and put
\begin{eqnarray}
S_\varepsilon^{\kappa,1}&:=&\{x\in\mathbb{R}^{N_1}\,, y\in\mathbb{R}^{N_2}\,:\,\, \kappa(\|x\|^2-R^2N_1)\geq \varepsilon N_1\,\}\,,\nonumber\\
S_\varepsilon^{\kappa,2}&:=&\{x\in\mathbb{R}^{N_1}\,, y\in\mathbb{R}^{N_2}\,:\,\, \kappa(\|y\|^2-R^2N_2)\geq \varepsilon N_2\,\}\,.\nonumber 
\end{eqnarray}
Thus $S_\varepsilon^c=\bigcup_{\kappa\in\{-1,1\},j\in\{1,2\}}S_\varepsilon^{\kappa,j}$. Moreover we pick $\eta>0$ small enough and set
\begin{eqnarray}
M^{(\kappa,j)}_i(\eta) &:=&
  \left( {\begin{array}{cc}
   a+(2-j)\kappa\eta & -\beta\sqrt{1-\alpha}\sigma_i \\
   -\beta\sqrt{1-\alpha}\sigma_i & b+(j-1)\kappa\eta \\
\end{array} } \right)\,,\quad i\in[N_1]\nonumber\\ 
M^{(\kappa,j)}_i(\eta)&:=&\mathrm{diag}(0,b+(j-1)\kappa\eta)\,,\quad i=N_1+1,\ldots , N_2\,.\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}




























Also, we put
\begin{eqnarray}
Z_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}^{\kappa,j}&:=& \exp\left(\frac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)+\frac{(2-j)N_1\kappa\eta a}{2}+\frac{(j-1)N_2\kappa\eta b}{2}-\eta \varepsilon N_j\right)\nonumber\\
&&\int_{S_\varepsilon^{\kappa,j}} \frac{dxdy}{|S_1||S_2|}\exp\left( -\frac 1 2 \sum_{i=1}^{N_2} (z_i^T,M^{(\kappa,j)}_i(\eta) z_i)\right)\nonumber\\
\end{eqnarray}
so that 
$$
(\ref{eq:II-termRBM})=-\sum_{\kappa\in\{-1,1\},j=1,2} Z_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}^{\kappa,j}\,. 
$$



We conclude that for any $\eta>0$ sufficiently small and $a,b$ with $ab>(1-\alpha)\beta^2\lambda_+$ 
\begin{equation}
\lim\sup_{N_1,N_2} \widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}\geq \max(\bar A(a,b), \{A_\varepsilon^{\kappa, j}(\eta; a,b)\}_{\kappa\in\{-1,1\},j\in\{1,2\}})\,,
\end{equation}
where 
\begin{eqnarray}
A_\varepsilon^{\kappa,j}(\eta; a,b)&:=&-\eta\varepsilon+\frac12\alpha a(R^2+(2-j)\kappa\eta)+\frac12(1-\alpha) b(R^2+(j-1)\kappa\eta)\nonumber\\
&-&\log R -\frac12-\frac{1-2\alpha}{2}\log (b+(j-1)\kappa\eta)\nonumber\\
&-&\frac\alpha2 \int \rho_{MP}(d\lambda;\alpha)\log((a+(2-j)\kappa\eta)(b+(j-1)\kappa\eta)- (1-\alpha)\beta^2\lambda)\,. \nonumber
\end{eqnarray}

In analogy with the proof of Theorem \ref{Th:HM-sfer} we define 
\begin{eqnarray}
\Delta_{\varepsilon}^{\kappa,j}(\eta)&:=&\bar A(a,b)-A_\varepsilon^{\kappa,j}(\eta; a,b)\nonumber\\
&=&\eta \varepsilon-(2-j)\kappa\frac{\eta\alpha a}{2}-(j-1)\kappa\frac{\eta(1-\alpha) b}{2}+\frac{1-2\alpha}{2}\log(b+(j-1)\kappa\eta)\nonumber\\
&+&\frac\alpha2 \int \rho_{MP}(d\lambda;\alpha)\log\left(\frac{(a+(2-j)\kappa\eta)(b+(j-1)\kappa\eta)- (1-\alpha)\beta^2\lambda}{ab-(1-\alpha)\beta^2\lambda}\right)\,.\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
We need to show that $\Delta_{\varepsilon}^{\kappa,j}(\eta)\geq0$ for $\eta>0$ small. As before, to do so it suffices to prove the derivative in the origin to be non-negative uniformly in $\varepsilon>0$. Bearing in mind (\ref{eq:grad1RBM}), (\ref{eq:grad2RBM}) we have
\begin{eqnarray}
\frac{d}{d\eta} \Delta_{\varepsilon}^{\kappa,j}(\eta)\big|_{\eta=0}&=&\varepsilon+(2-j)\kappa\left(-\frac{a\alpha R^2}{2}+\frac\alpha2 \int \rho_{MP}(d\lambda;\alpha)\left(\frac{b}{ab-(1-\alpha)\beta^2\lambda}\right)\right)\nonumber\\
&+&(j-1)\kappa\left(-\frac{b(1-\alpha) R^2}{2}+\frac{1-2\alpha}{2b}+\frac\alpha2 \int \rho_{MP}(d\lambda;\alpha)\left(\frac{a}{ab-(1-\alpha)\beta^2\lambda}\right)\right)\nonumber\\
&=&\varepsilon-(2-j)\kappa\partial_a\bar A-(j-1)\kappa\partial_b\bar A\geq0\,. \nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
Since the inequality must hold for any $\varepsilon>0$, $\kappa\in\{-1,1\}$ and $j\in\{1,2\}$, we have to pick $(\bar a, \bar b)=\arg\min \bar A$. Therefore 
$$
\lim\sup_{N_1,N_2} A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}\geq \max(\bar A(\bar a,\bar b), \{A^{\varepsilon,\kappa_1,\kappa_2}(\eta; \bar a,\bar b)\}_{\kappa_1,\kappa_2\in\{-1,1\}})= \min_{ab>\beta^2(1-\alpha)\lambda_+}\bar A( a, b)\quad \forall \varepsilon>0\,,
$$
which combined with (\ref{eq:upperbound.RBM}) proves the theorem.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.2
nodes.statement:
Let $a>\lambda_+$ and set for brevity $\lambda^*:=\max_{i\in[N_1]}\lambda_i$. We write
$$
\frac{1}{N_1+N_2}E[\log Z_{N_1,N_2}]=\sum_{k\geq0}E\left[\frac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log Z_{N_1,N_2}\,|\,\,(k+1)a\geq \lambda^*> ka\right ]P((k+1)a\geq \lambda^*> ka)\,. 
$$
Inside the conditional expectation we can bound
$
H_N(z)\leq a\|z\|^2\, 
$. Therefore
\begin{eqnarray}
E\left[\frac{1}{N_1+N_2} \log Z_{N_1,N_2}\,|\,\,(k+1)a\geq \lambda^*> ka\right]&\leq& \frac{1}{N_1+N_2} \log\int\gamma_{N_1,\theta}(dx) \exp\left(\|x\|^2(\beta a(k+1))-Nr\left(\frac{\|x\|}{\sqrt N}\right)\right)\nonumber\\
&\leq&\frac{1}{N_1+N_2}\max_{R\geq0}\left(R^2(\beta a(k+1))-N_1r\left(\frac{R}{\sqrt N_1}\right)\right)\,\nonumber\\
&=&\max_{R\geq0}\left(R^2(\beta a(k+1))-r\left(R\right)\right)\,.\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
On the other hand by assumption
\begin{equation}
P((k+1)a\geq \lambda^*> ka)\leq 2e^{-ca^2k^2N_1}\,,\quad c>0\,. 
\end{equation}
In conclusion
\begin{equation}
E[A_{N_1,N_2}]\leq \sum_{k\geq0}e^{-ca^2k^2N_1}\max_{R\geq0}\left(R^2(\beta a(k+1))-r\left(R\right)\right)=:f(a,\beta)\,,
\end{equation}
a continuous bounded function. In particular the estimate holds also for $a\to\lambda_+$.
nodes.statement_short: Condition on the top eigenvalue lying in $(ka,(k+1)a]$, bound each conditional free energy by a radial maximum, and sum against Gaussian tail probabilities.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.1
nodes.statement:
Now we are ready to prove the Legendre equivalences of Theorem \ref{th:main}. We shall prove only (\ref{eq:mainHM}), (\ref{eq:mainRBM1}), (\ref{eq:mainRBM2}); the dual relations (\ref{eq:mainHM-dual}), (\ref{eq:mainRBM1-dual}), (\ref{eq:mainRBM2-dual}) then follow directly, as one can easily verify the inverse Legendre transformation to be also well defined and involutive. 

We start by $i)$, where we deal with a single Gaussian prior. 
Let $\varepsilon>0$, $\delta>0$. From now on we will systematically omit the dependence on $\delta$ of the objects we will operate with. Let further $r<N_1^{\delta}/\varepsilon$, $R_0:=0$, $R_{r+1}:=N_1^{\delta}$, $\{R_i\}_{i=1,\ldots,r}\subset[0,N_1^{\delta})$ with $|R_{i+1}-R_i|<2\varepsilon$, and decompose
$
\mathbb{R}^{N_1}:=\bigcup_{i=0}^rS^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}\cup T
$, where 
$$
S^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}:=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^{N_1}\,\:\, R_i\sqrt{N_1}\leq \|z\|_2\leq R_{i+1}\sqrt{N_1}\}\,,\quad T:=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^{N_1}\,\:\, \|z\|_2\geq {N_1}^{\delta+\frac12}\}\,.
$$
Comparing with (\ref{eq:Sfshell}) one easily sees that the $S^{[i]}_{\varepsilon,N_1}$ are spherical shells. We denote by $\sigma^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}$ the uniform distributions on  these shells. 
Then we have
\begin{equation} Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_1}=\sum_{i=0}^r Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2}[i]+\tilde Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2}\,,
\end{equation}
where
$$
Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2}[i]:=\int_{S^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}}\rho_{N_1}(dx)e^{-\beta H_{N_1,N_2}(x)}\,,\quad \tilde Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2}:=\int_{T}\rho_{N_1}(dx)e^{-\beta H_{N_1,N_2}(x)}\,.
$$
The tail term $\tilde Z^\rho_{N_1,N_2}$ gives a negligible contribution thanks to Lemma \ref{lemma:coda} and we will ignore it all the time.
Thus by (\ref{eq:dec}) we get 
$$
\max_{i\in[r]} Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2}[i]\leq Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2,\beta}\leq \frac{N^{\delta}}{\varepsilon}\max_{i\in[r]} Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2}[i]\,.
$$
Therefore setting
\begin{equation} A_{N_1,N_2}[i]:=\left(\frac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2}[i]\right)
\end{equation}
we have
\begin{equation} \max_{i\in[r]}\left(A_{N_1,N_2}[i]\right)\leq \frac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2}\leq \max_{i\in[r]}\left(A_{N_1,N_2}[i]\right)+\frac{\delta\log N_1-\log \varepsilon}{N_1+N_2}\,. 
\end{equation}
So the free energy of $HM_{\rho}$ is given by the limit of $\max_{i\in[r]}\left(A_{N_1,N_2}[i]\right)$, provided it exists. 


We notice now that by continuity for any $x\in S^{[i]}_{\varepsilon,N_1}$
\begin{equation} \frac{\|x\|^2}{2\theta}+N_1r\left(\frac{\|x\|}{\sqrt N_1}\right)=\frac{\tilde R_i^2N_1}{2\theta}+N_1r\left(\tilde R_i\right)+\OOO{\varepsilon} 
\end{equation}
where $\tilde R_i\in[R_i, R_{i+1}]$. Therefore
\begin{equation}
Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2,\beta}[i]=e^{-\frac{\tilde R_i^2N_1}{2\theta}-N_1r\left(\tilde R_i \right)-\OOO{\varepsilon}}\frac{|S^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}|}{\sqrt{2\pi\theta}^{N_1}}\int \sigma^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}(dx)e^{-\beta H_{N_1,N_2}(x)}\,
\end{equation}
and
\begin{eqnarray}
A_{N_1,N_2}[i]&=&\frac{N_1}{N_1+N_2}\left(\frac{1}{N_1}\log\left(\frac{|S^{[i]}_{\varepsilon,N_1}|}{\sqrt{2\pi\theta}^{N_1}}\right)-\frac{\tilde R_i^2}{2\theta }-r\left(\tilde R_i\right)\right)+\widehat A_{N_1,N_2}^{\varepsilon}\left(\tilde R_i\right)+\frac{\OOO{\varepsilon}}{N_1+N_2}\nonumber\\
&=:&\tilde A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}\left(\tilde R_i\right)+\frac{\OOO{\varepsilon}}{N_1+N_2}\nonumber\,.
\end{eqnarray}
Thus we see that the existence of the thermodynamic limit is ensured by Lemma \ref{lemma-gusci} and we have

$$
\lim_{N_1,N_2}\max_{i\in[r]}\left(A_{N_1,N_2}[i]\right)=\sup_{R>0}\lim_{N_1,N_2}\left(\tilde A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}(R)\right)=:\sup_{R>0}\tilde A_\varepsilon(R)\,. 
$$
By the uniform concavity of $\tilde A_\varepsilon(R)$ we have
$$
\lim_{\varepsilon\to0}\sup_{R>0}\tilde A_\varepsilon(R)=\sup_{R>0}\lim_{\varepsilon\to0}\tilde A_\varepsilon(R)=-\frac{\alpha}{2}\log\theta+\alpha\sup_{R>0}\left(\log R+\frac12+\alpha^{-1}A_{\sigma}(R,\beta)-r(R)-\frac{R^2}{2\theta}\right)\,
$$
and the proof of (\ref{eq:mainHM}) is concluded. 

\

Note that in this argument the regularising function $r$ plays essentially no role. So it can be set to zero and repeat verbatim all the previous steps for the $RBM_{\sigma,\gamma}$. This way we obtain (\ref{eq:mainRBM1}). 

\

Finally we turn to $RBM_{\rho^2}$. Here we have to slice up both Gaussian priors and the previous construction easily extends. We just sketch the argument, stressing only the points in which it differs from above. Let $\varepsilon>0$, $\delta>0$, $r<N_1^{\delta}/\varepsilon$, $r'<N_2^{\delta}/\varepsilon$, $R_0,R'_0:=0$, $R_{r+1}:=N_1^{\delta}$, $R'_{r'+1}:=N_2^{\delta}$, $\{R_i\}_{i=1,\ldots,r}\subset[0,N_1^{\delta})$ with $|R_{i+1}-R_i|<2\varepsilon$, $\{R'_i\}_{i=1,\ldots,r'}\subset[0,N_2^{\delta})$ with $|R'_{i+1}-R'_i|<2\varepsilon$. Decompose
$
\mathbb{R}^{N_1}\times \mathbb{R}^{N_2}:=\bigcup_{i\in[r], j\in[r']}S_{N_1,\varepsilon}^{[i]}\times {S'}_{N_2,\varepsilon}^{[j]} \cup T
$, where 
\begin{eqnarray}
S^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}&:=&\{z\in\mathbb{R}^{N_1}\,\:\, R_i\sqrt{N_1}\leq \|z\|_2\leq R_{i+1}\sqrt{N_1}\}\,,\nonumber\\
{S'}^{[i]}_{N_2,\varepsilon}&:=&\{z\in\mathbb{R}^{N_2}\,\:\, R'_i\sqrt{N_2}\leq \|z\|_2\leq R'_{i+1}\sqrt{N_2}\}\,,\nonumber\\
T&:=&\{z\in\mathbb{R}^{N_1}\,\:\, \|z\|_2\geq {N_1}^{\delta+\frac12}\}\cup \{z\in\mathbb{R}^{N_2}\,\:\, \|z\|_2\geq {N_2}^{\delta+\frac12}\}\,.\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}

Again $T$ can be neglected due to Lemma \ref{lemma:coda}. We have to evaluate
\begin{eqnarray}
&&Z^{\rho^2}_{N_1,N_2}[i,j]:=\int_{S^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}\times {S'}_{N_2,\varepsilon}^{[j]}}\rho^2_{N_1N_2}(dxdy)e^{-\beta H_{N_1,N_2}(x,y)}\,,\nonumber\\
&=&\frac{|S^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}\times {S'}_{N_2,\varepsilon}^{[j]}|}{\sqrt{2\pi\theta}^{N_1+N_2}} e^{-\frac{\tilde R^2_iN_1+{R'}^2_jN_2}{2\theta}-\sqrt{N_1N_2}r\left(\tilde{R}_i, \tilde{R'}_j\right)+\OOO{\varepsilon}} \int_{S^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}\times {S'}_{N_1,\varepsilon}^{[j]}}\sigma^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}(dx)\sigma^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}(dy) e^{-\beta H_{N_1,N_2}(x,y)}\,,\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
where the $\tilde R_i$ and $\tilde {R'}_i$ are introduced as before (see (\ref{eq:Rtilde})). Therefore

\begin{eqnarray}
A_{N_1,N_2,\beta}[i,j]&:=&\frac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log Z^{\rho^2}_{N_1,N_2,\beta}[i,j]\nonumber\\
&=&\frac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log\left(\frac{|S^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}\times {S'}_{N_2,\varepsilon}^{[j]}|}{\sqrt{2\pi\theta}^{N_1+N_2}}\right)+\frac{\OOO{\varepsilon}}{N_1+N_2} -\frac{\tilde R^2_i+{R'}^2_j}{2\theta}\nonumber\\
&-&\frac{\sqrt{N_1N_2}}{N_1+N_2}r\left(\tilde R_i, \tilde {R'}_j\right)+\widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}(\tilde R_i, \tilde R_j)\nonumber\,,
\end{eqnarray}
where $\widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}(\tilde R_i, \tilde {R'}_j)$ is the free energy of the RBM whose priors are the spherical shell measures of centres $\tilde R_i, \tilde {R'}_j$. The argument to pass to the thermodynamic limit is then the same, so (\ref{eq:mainRBM2}) is obtained.
nodes.statement_short: Slice the Gaussian prior into thin spherical shells, discard the tail by Lemma 3.4, and take the maximum over shells (Laplace method). The shell free energies converge to spherical ones by Lemma 2.3, giving a sup over radii.

nodes.name: Notation
nodes.statement: In this proof we write $N$ to mean $N_1$ or $N_2$ and by $A^{\sigma}(R; \beta)$ the free energy of a spherical model of radius $R$, according to the context. No further details are needed.
nodes.statement_short: Fix notation for layer size and spherical free energy.

nodes.name: Mean value radius
nodes.statement:
By Fubini and the mean value theorem there is a $R^*_\varepsilon\in[R\sqrt N-\varepsilon,R\sqrt N+\varepsilon]$ for which
$$
\widehat A_{N_1,N_2}=A_{N_1,N_2}^{\sigma}(R^*_\varepsilon; \beta)\,. 
$$
nodes.statement_short: Fubini and mean value theorem give a radius $R^*_\varepsilon$ in the shell.

nodes.name: Rescale radius into temperature
nodes.statement:
By a simple change of variables we have
$$
A_{N_1,N_2}^{\sigma}(R^*_\varepsilon; \beta)=A_{N_1,N_2}^{\sigma}(R; c_{N,\varepsilon}\beta)\,, 
$$
with $c_{N,\varepsilon}:=R^2_\varepsilon/R^2N$.
nodes.statement_short: Change of variables moves the radius into $\beta$.

nodes.name: Lipschitz bound
nodes.statement:
Therefore by Lipschitz continuity of the free energy w.r.t. $\beta$
$$
|A^\sigma_{N_1,N_2}-\widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}|\leq \frac\varepsilon N\,. 
$$
nodes.statement_short: Lipschitz continuity in $\beta$ gives an $\varepsilon/N$ bound.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: This, combined with $A^\sigma_{N_1,N_2}=\lim_{\varepsilon\to0} \widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}$, gives the assert.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude commutation of limits.

nodes.name: Upper bound
nodes.statement:
Let $2q>\beta(1-\alpha)\lambda_+$. Then using (\ref{eq:shells-surface}) we have 
\begin{eqnarray}
\varepsilon \hat{Z}_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}(\beta,\alpha,R)&=& \varepsilon\ e^{q R^2 N_1}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{N_1}}\sigma_{N_1,R,\varepsilon}(dz)e^{-\sum_i^{N_1}(q-\frac{\beta(1-\alpha)}{2}\lambda_i)z_i^2} \\
&\leq&e^{q R^2 N_1}\frac{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}2}}{|S_{R\sqrt{N_1}}|}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}\frac{dz}{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}2}} e^{-\sum_i^{N_1}(2q-\beta(1-\alpha)\lambda_i)z_i^2/2}\nonumber\\
&=&e^{q R^2 N_1}\frac{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}2}}{|S_{R\sqrt{N}}|}e^{-\frac 12\sum_i^N\log(2q-\beta(1-\alpha)\lambda_i)}\nonumber\,,
\end{eqnarray}
therefore, since $\frac 1{N_1} \log \left(|S_{R\sqrt{N_1}}| /\sqrt{2\pi}^{N_1}  \right) \to \log R +\frac 1 2$ and thanks to Lemma \ref{lemma-gusci} 
$$
\lim\sup_{N_1,N_2}\frac1{N_1+N_2} \log Z_{N_1,N_2}(\beta,\alpha,R)\leq \alpha q R^2 -\frac \alpha2\int\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)\log(2q-\beta(1-\alpha)\lambda)-\alpha\log R-\frac\alpha2=:\tilde A(q)\,,
$$
whence, as $\tilde A(q)$ is continuous, 
$$
\lim\sup_{N_1,N_2}\frac{1}{N_1+N_2} \log Z_{N_1,N_2}(\beta,\alpha,R)\leq\min_{2q\geq\beta(1-\alpha)\lambda_+}\tilde A(q).
$$
nodes.statement_short: Relax the shell with a Lagrange multiplier $q$ to a Gaussian integral, giving $\limsup\le\min_q\tilde A(q)$.

nodes.name: Convexity of $\tilde A$
nodes.statement:
Moreover for $2q>\beta(1-\alpha)\lambda_+$
$$
\partial_q^2 \tilde A(q)=2\alpha\int d\lambda\frac{\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)}{(2q-\beta(1-\alpha)\lambda)^2}>0,
$$
thus $\tilde A(q)$ is  convex and the minimum is attained in a unique point $\bar q$.
nodes.statement_short: Second derivative positive, so a unique minimiser $\bar q$.

nodes.name: Reverse bound setup
nodes.statement:
\noindent Now the reverse bound. Let $\varepsilon>0$ and $S^c_{N_1,R,\varepsilon}$ the complementary set of the shell $S_{N_1,R,\varepsilon}$. It holds
$$
\varepsilon \widehat Z_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}=e^{ q R^2 N_1}\frac{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}{2}}}{|S_{R\sqrt{N_1}}|}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{N_1}}\frac{dz}{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}{2}}} e^{-\sum_i^{N_1}(q-\frac{\beta(1-\alpha)}{2}\lambda_i)z_i^2}-e^{ q R^2 N_1}\frac{(2\pi)^{\frac N2}}{|S_{R\sqrt{N_1}}|}\int_{S_{N_1,R,\varepsilon}^c}\frac{dz}{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}2}} e^{-\sum_i^{N_1}(q-\frac{\beta(1-\alpha)}{2}\lambda_i)z_i^2}.
$$
nodes.statement_short: Write the shell integral as full Gaussian minus complement of shell.

nodes.name: Bound complement of the shell
nodes.statement_short: Exponential Chebyshev bound with shifted multipliers $q\pm\eta$ on the complement.

nodes.name: Lower bound by maximum
nodes.statement_short: At scale $\varepsilon=\tilde\varepsilon N$ the liminf is bounded below by the max of three functionals.

nodes.name: Minimiser dominates
nodes.statement:
Now we show that if $\bar q$ is the unique minimiser of $\tilde A(q)$ it is for $\eta$ small enough
$$
\tilde A(\bar q)=\max\left(\tilde A(\bar q), A^1_{\tilde\varepsilon}(\eta; \bar q), A^2_{\tilde\varepsilon}(\eta; \bar q)\right)\,,
$$
which will conclude the proof.

To do so we introduce
\begin{eqnarray}
\Delta_-(q;\eta)&:=&\tilde A(q)-A^1_{\tilde\varepsilon}(\eta; q)= -\alpha\eta(R^2-\tilde\varepsilon)+\frac\alpha2\int d\lambda\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)\log\left(\frac{2(q+\eta)-\beta\lambda}{2q-\beta\lambda}\right);\\
\Delta_+(q;\eta)&:=&\tilde A(q)-A^2_{\tilde\varepsilon}(\eta; q)= \alpha\eta(R^2+\tilde\varepsilon)+\frac\alpha2\int d\lambda\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)\log\left(\frac{2(q-\eta)-\beta\lambda}{2q-\beta\lambda}\right)\,.
\end{eqnarray}
\noindent As a function of $\eta$, $\Delta_\pm(q;\eta)$ are continuous and differentiable, vanishing in $\eta=0$ and with $\lim_{\eta\to+\infty}\Delta_\pm(q,\eta)=\pm\infty$. Moreover $\Delta_+(q;\eta)$ is uniformly convex and $\Delta_-(q;\eta)$ uniformly concave. Thus $\Delta_-(q;\eta)$ assumes a positive maximum iff the derivative in $\eta=0$ is positive, that is
\begin{equation} 0<-(R^2-\tilde\varepsilon)+\int d\lambda\frac{\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)}{2q-\beta\lambda}=\tilde \varepsilon-\partial_q \tilde A(q)\,.
\end{equation}

\noindent Likewise for $\Delta_+(q;\eta)$ is always positive iff 
$\left.\partial_\eta \Delta_+(q;\eta)\right|_{\eta=0}\geq0$, \textit{i.e. }
\begin{equation} 0\leq(R^2+\tilde\varepsilon)+\int d\lambda\frac{\rho_{MP}(\lambda;\alpha)}{2q-\beta\lambda}=\tilde \varepsilon+\partial_q \tilde A(q).
\end{equation}
Combining (\ref{eq:upper-bound-epsi1}) and (\ref{eq:upper-bound-epsi2}) we get
$$
-\tilde\varepsilon\leq \left.\partial_q \tilde A(q)\right|_{q=\tilde q}<\tilde\varepsilon\,,,
$$
that is $\tilde q$ is the unique stationary point of $\tilde A(q)$.
nodes.statement_short: Show $\tilde A(\bar q)$ dominates the off-shell terms for small $\eta$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement_short: Letting $\tilde\varepsilon\to0$ gives the formula.

nodes.name: Define $\Delta_\pm$
nodes.statement_short: Introduce differences $\Delta_\pm$ of the competing functionals.

nodes.name: Condition for $\Delta_-$
nodes.statement_short: Concavity reduces positivity of $\Delta_-$ to a derivative condition at $\eta=0$.

nodes.name: Condition for $\Delta_+$
nodes.statement_short: Same derivative condition for $\Delta_+$.

nodes.name: Stationary point
nodes.statement:
Combining (\ref{eq:upper-bound-epsi1}) and (\ref{eq:upper-bound-epsi2}) we get
$$
-\tilde\varepsilon\leq \left.\partial_q \tilde A(q)\right|_{q=\tilde q}<\tilde\varepsilon\,,,
$$
that is $\tilde q$ is the unique stationary point of $\tilde A(q)$.
nodes.statement_short: The two conditions force $q$ to be the stationary point of $\tilde A$.

nodes.name: Split expectation
nodes.statement:
For any $a>\bar\sigma$ we compute
$$
E[e^{\alpha\beta\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i\tilde x_i\tilde y_i}]=E[e^{\beta\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i\tilde x_i\tilde y_i}1_{\{\max_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i\leq a\}}]+E[e^{\beta\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i\tilde x_i\tilde y_i}1_{\{\max_{i\in[N_1]}\sigma_i>a\}}]\,.
$$
nodes.statement_short: Split by whether the top singular value exceeds $a$.

nodes.name: Bound first summand
nodes.statement_short: Bound the small-singular-value part.

nodes.name: Bound second summand
nodes.statement_short: Bound the large-singular-value part as in earlier work.

nodes.name: Annealed bound
nodes.statement_short: Combine into an annealed bound on the free energy.

nodes.name: Conclude via spectral tail
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz-type bound plus spectral concentration (P2).

nodes.name: Gaussian representation
nodes.statement:
Now  start from (\ref{eq:diagRBM}) and write for any $a,b$ such that $ab>\beta^2(1-\alpha)\lambda_+$
\begin{eqnarray}
Z_{N_1,N_2}&=&\int\sigma_1(dx)\sigma_2(dy) \exp\left( \sqrt{1-\alpha} \beta\sum_{i\in[N_1]}x_iy_i\sigma_i-\frac a2 \|x\|^2-\frac b2 \|y\|^2+\frac a2 R^2N_1+\frac b2 R^2N_2\right)\nonumber\\
&=&\exp\left(\frac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)\right) \int\sigma_1(dx)\sigma_2(dy)\exp\left( -\frac 1 2 \sum_{i=1}^{N_2} (z_i^T,M_i z_i)\right) \,,
\end{eqnarray}
where we have defined 
$$
z^T_i := \begin{cases}
(x_i,y_i)&i=1,\ldots , N_1\,,\\
(0,y_i)&i=N_1+1,\ldots , N_2
\end{cases}$$
and the $2\times 2$ symmetric positively defined matrix 
$$
M_i :=
  \left( {\begin{array}{cc}
   a & -\beta\sqrt{1-\alpha}\sigma_i \\
   -\beta\sqrt{1-\alpha}\sigma_i & b \\
\end{array} } \right)\,,\quad i\in[N_1]\qquad M_i:=\mathrm{diag}(0,b)\,,\quad i=N_1+1,\ldots , N_2\,.
$$
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite $Z$ with multipliers $a,b$ as a product of $2\times2$ quadratic forms.

nodes.name: Upper bound via Gaussian integral
nodes.statement_short: Bound the shell partition function by the explicit Gaussian integral.

nodes.name: Trial function
nodes.statement:
We introduce
\begin{equation} \bar A(a,b):= \frac {R^2}{2} (a\alpha+b(1-\alpha))-\log R-\frac12-\frac{1-2\alpha}{2}\log b -\frac{\alpha}{2}\int \rho_{MP}(d\lambda;\alpha)\log(ab-(1-\alpha)\beta^2\lambda)\,.
\end{equation}
and 
$$
\lim\sup_{N_1,N_2}A_{N_1,N_2}\leq \bar A(a,b)\,,\quad \forall a,b>0\,:\,\,ab>(1-\alpha)\beta^2\lambda_+\,. 
$$
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $\bar A(a,b)$ bounding the limsup.

nodes.name: Upper bound by minimum
nodes.statement_short: Joint convexity gives $\limsup\le\min\bar A$.

nodes.name: Gradient of $\bar A$
nodes.statement_short: Record the partial derivatives of $\bar A$.

nodes.name: Reverse bound setup
nodes.statement:
For the reverse bound consider again  spherical shells around $S_{R,N_1}$ and $S_{R,N_2}$ of thickness $\varepsilon$, that we name respectively $S_{1,\varepsilon}$ and $S_{2,\varepsilon}$. We split $S_{1,\varepsilon}=\mathbb{R}^{N_1}\setminus S^c_{1,\varepsilon}$ and $S_{2,\varepsilon}=\mathbb{R}^{N_2}\setminus S^c_{2,\varepsilon}$ and set $S_{\varepsilon}:=S_{1,\varepsilon}\times S_{2,\varepsilon}$. We have

\begin{eqnarray}
\varepsilon^2 \widehat Z_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}&:=&\varepsilon^2\int\sigma_{N_1, R,\varepsilon}(dx)\sigma_{N_2,R,\varepsilon}(dy)e^{-\beta H_N(x,y)}\nonumber\\
&=&\exp\left(\frac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)\right) \int_{\mathbb{R}^{N_1}\times \mathbb{R}^{N_2}} \frac{dxdy}{|S_1||S_2|}\exp\left( -\frac 1 2 \sum_{i=1}^{N_2} (z_i^T,M_i z_i)\right)\nonumber\\
&-&\exp\left(\frac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)\right) \int_{S^c_{\varepsilon}} \frac{dxdy}{|S_1||S_2|}\exp\left( -\frac 1 2 \sum_{i=1}^{N_2} (z_i^T,M_i z_i)\right) \,,
\end{eqnarray}
where we used again the representation (\ref{eq:repr-Z-RBM}). The free energy associated to the first summand was already computed above in the thermodynamic limit. Therefore we have to upper bound the second summand.
nodes.statement_short: Split the shell integral into full space minus complement.

nodes.name: Decompose complement
nodes.statement_short: Cover the complement by four half-spaces in $\|x\|^2,\|y\|^2$ and shift multipliers by $\pm\eta$.

nodes.name: Lower bound by maximum
nodes.statement_short: Bound the shell free energy below by the max of $\bar A$ and four off-shell functionals.

nodes.name: Derivative of differences
nodes.statement_short: Positivity of $\Delta^{\kappa,j}_\varepsilon$ reduces to its derivative at $\eta=0$, expressed via the gradient of $\bar A$.

nodes.name: Conclude at argmin
nodes.statement:
Since the inequality must hold for any $\varepsilon>0$, $\kappa\in\{-1,1\}$ and $j\in\{1,2\}$, we have to pick $(\bar a, \bar b)=\arg\min \bar A$. Therefore 
$$
\lim\sup_{N_1,N_2} A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}\geq \max(\bar A(\bar a,\bar b), \{A^{\varepsilon,\kappa_1,\kappa_2}(\eta; \bar a,\bar b)\}_{\kappa_1,\kappa_2\in\{-1,1\}})= \min_{ab>\beta^2(1-\alpha)\lambda_+}\bar A( a, b)\quad \forall \varepsilon>0\,,
$$
which combined with (\ref{eq:upperbound.RBM}) proves the theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Choosing $(\bar a,\bar b)=\arg\min\bar A$ matches the upper bound.

nodes.name: Condition on top eigenvalue
nodes.statement:
Let $a>\lambda_+$ and set for brevity $\lambda^*:=\max_{i\in[N_1]}\lambda_i$. We write
$$
\frac{1}{N_1+N_2}E[\log Z_{N_1,N_2}]=\sum_{k\geq0}E\left[\frac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log Z_{N_1,N_2}\,|\,\,(k+1)a\geq \lambda^*> ka\right ]P((k+1)a\geq \lambda^*> ka)\,. 
$$
nodes.statement_short: Decompose by the range of the top eigenvalue.

nodes.name: Conditional bound
nodes.statement:
Inside the conditional expectation we can bound
$
H_N(z)\leq a\|z\|^2\, 
$. Therefore
\begin{eqnarray}
E\left[\frac{1}{N_1+N_2} \log Z_{N_1,N_2}\,|\,\,(k+1)a\geq \lambda^*> ka\right]&\leq& \frac{1}{N_1+N_2} \log\int\gamma_{N_1,\theta}(dx) \exp\left(\|x\|^2(\beta a(k+1))-Nr\left(\frac{\|x\|}{\sqrt N}\right)\right)\nonumber\\
&\leq&\frac{1}{N_1+N_2}\max_{R\geq0}\left(R^2(\beta a(k+1))-N_1r\left(\frac{R}{\sqrt N_1}\right)\right)\,\nonumber\\
&=&\max_{R\geq0}\left(R^2(\beta a(k+1))-r\left(R\right)\right)\,.\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Bound each conditional free energy by a radial maximum.

nodes.name: Tail probability
nodes.statement_short: Gaussian tail for the top eigenvalue.

nodes.name: Sum up
nodes.statement_short: Summing gives a continuous bounded $f$.

nodes.name: Reduce to (3.5)
nodes.statement: We prove only (\ref{eq:coda1}), as (\ref{eq:coda2}), (\ref{eq:coda3}) are similar.
nodes.statement_short: Only the first bound is proved.

nodes.name: Extract Gaussian factor
nodes.statement_short: Bound the tail integral by $e^{-R^2N^{1+\delta}/2\theta}Z(2\theta)$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Then (\ref{eq:coda1}) follows from Lemma \ref{lemma:apriori-bound-HM}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the a priori bound.

nodes.name: Reduction to primal formulas
nodes.statement: Now we are ready to prove the Legendre equivalences of Theorem \ref{th:main}. We shall prove only (\ref{eq:mainHM}), (\ref{eq:mainRBM1}), (\ref{eq:mainRBM2}); the dual relations (\ref{eq:mainHM-dual}), (\ref{eq:mainRBM1-dual}), (\ref{eq:mainRBM2-dual}) then follow directly, as one can easily verify the inverse Legendre transformation to be also well defined and involutive.
nodes.statement_short: Only the primal formulas are proved; duals follow by involutivity of the Legendre transform.

nodes.name: Part i)
nodes.statement:
We start by $i)$, where we deal with a single Gaussian prior. 
Let $\varepsilon>0$, $\delta>0$. From now on we will systematically omit the dependence on $\delta$ of the objects we will operate with. Let further $r<N_1^{\delta}/\varepsilon$, $R_0:=0$, $R_{r+1}:=N_1^{\delta}$, $\{R_i\}_{i=1,\ldots,r}\subset[0,N_1^{\delta})$ with $|R_{i+1}-R_i|<2\varepsilon$, and decompose
$
\mathbb{R}^{N_1}:=\bigcup_{i=0}^rS^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}\cup T
$, where 
$$
S^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}:=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^{N_1}\,\:\, R_i\sqrt{N_1}\leq \|z\|_2\leq R_{i+1}\sqrt{N_1}\}\,,\quad T:=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^{N_1}\,\:\, \|z\|_2\geq {N_1}^{\delta+\frac12}\}\,.
$$
Comparing with (\ref{eq:Sfshell}) one easily sees that the $S^{[i]}_{\varepsilon,N_1}$ are spherical shells. We denote by $\sigma^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}$ the uniform distributions on  these shells. 
Then we have
\begin{equation} Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_1}=\sum_{i=0}^r Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2}[i]+\tilde Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2}\,,
\end{equation}
where
$$
Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2}[i]:=\int_{S^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}}\rho_{N_1}(dx)e^{-\beta H_{N_1,N_2}(x)}\,,\quad \tilde Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2}:=\int_{T}\rho_{N_1}(dx)e^{-\beta H_{N_1,N_2}(x)}\,.
$$
The tail term $\tilde Z^\rho_{N_1,N_2}$ gives a negligible contribution thanks to Lemma \ref{lemma:coda} and we will ignore it all the time.
Thus by (\ref{eq:dec}) we get 
$$
\max_{i\in[r]} Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2}[i]\leq Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2,\beta}\leq \frac{N^{\delta}}{\varepsilon}\max_{i\in[r]} Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2}[i]\,.
$$
Therefore setting
\begin{equation} A_{N_1,N_2}[i]:=\left(\frac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2}[i]\right)
\end{equation}
we have
\begin{equation} \max_{i\in[r]}\left(A_{N_1,N_2}[i]\right)\leq \frac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2}\leq \max_{i\in[r]}\left(A_{N_1,N_2}[i]\right)+\frac{\delta\log N_1-\log \varepsilon}{N_1+N_2}\,. 
\end{equation}
So the free energy of $HM_{\rho}$ is given by the limit of $\max_{i\in[r]}\left(A_{N_1,N_2}[i]\right)$, provided it exists. 


We notice now that by continuity for any $x\in S^{[i]}_{\varepsilon,N_1}$
\begin{equation} \frac{\|x\|^2}{2\theta}+N_1r\left(\frac{\|x\|}{\sqrt N_1}\right)=\frac{\tilde R_i^2N_1}{2\theta}+N_1r\left(\tilde R_i\right)+\OOO{\varepsilon} 
\end{equation}
where $\tilde R_i\in[R_i, R_{i+1}]$. Therefore
\begin{equation}
Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2,\beta}[i]=e^{-\frac{\tilde R_i^2N_1}{2\theta}-N_1r\left(\tilde R_i \right)-\OOO{\varepsilon}}\frac{|S^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}|}{\sqrt{2\pi\theta}^{N_1}}\int \sigma^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}(dx)e^{-\beta H_{N_1,N_2}(x)}\,
\end{equation}
and
\begin{eqnarray}
A_{N_1,N_2}[i]&=&\frac{N_1}{N_1+N_2}\left(\frac{1}{N_1}\log\left(\frac{|S^{[i]}_{\varepsilon,N_1}|}{\sqrt{2\pi\theta}^{N_1}}\right)-\frac{\tilde R_i^2}{2\theta }-r\left(\tilde R_i\right)\right)+\widehat A_{N_1,N_2}^{\varepsilon}\left(\tilde R_i\right)+\frac{\OOO{\varepsilon}}{N_1+N_2}\nonumber\\
&=:&\tilde A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}\left(\tilde R_i\right)+\frac{\OOO{\varepsilon}}{N_1+N_2}\nonumber\,.
\end{eqnarray}
Thus we see that the existence of the thermodynamic limit is ensured by Lemma \ref{lemma-gusci} and we have

$$
\lim_{N_1,N_2}\max_{i\in[r]}\left(A_{N_1,N_2}[i]\right)=\sup_{R>0}\lim_{N_1,N_2}\left(\tilde A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}(R)\right)=:\sup_{R>0}\tilde A_\varepsilon(R)\,. 
$$
By the uniform concavity of $\tilde A_\varepsilon(R)$ we have
$$
\lim_{\varepsilon\to0}\sup_{R>0}\tilde A_\varepsilon(R)=\sup_{R>0}\lim_{\varepsilon\to0}\tilde A_\varepsilon(R)=-\frac{\alpha}{2}\log\theta+\alpha\sup_{R>0}\left(\log R+\frac12+\alpha^{-1}A_{\sigma}(R,\beta)-r(R)-\frac{R^2}{2\theta}\right)\,
$$
and the proof of (\ref{eq:mainHM}) is concluded.
nodes.statement_short: Prove the $HM_\sigma\leftrightarrow HM_\rho$ formula by shell slicing.

nodes.name: Part ii)
nodes.statement: Note that in this argument the regularising function $r$ plays essentially no role. So it can be set to zero and repeat verbatim all the previous steps for the $RBM_{\sigma,\gamma}$. This way we obtain (\ref{eq:mainRBM1}).
nodes.statement_short: Set $r=0$ and repeat for $RBM_{\sigma,\gamma}$.

nodes.name: Part iii)
nodes.statement:
Finally we turn to $RBM_{\rho^2}$. Here we have to slice up both Gaussian priors and the previous construction easily extends. We just sketch the argument, stressing only the points in which it differs from above. Let $\varepsilon>0$, $\delta>0$, $r<N_1^{\delta}/\varepsilon$, $r'<N_2^{\delta}/\varepsilon$, $R_0,R'_0:=0$, $R_{r+1}:=N_1^{\delta}$, $R'_{r'+1}:=N_2^{\delta}$, $\{R_i\}_{i=1,\ldots,r}\subset[0,N_1^{\delta})$ with $|R_{i+1}-R_i|<2\varepsilon$, $\{R'_i\}_{i=1,\ldots,r'}\subset[0,N_2^{\delta})$ with $|R'_{i+1}-R'_i|<2\varepsilon$. Decompose
$
\mathbb{R}^{N_1}\times \mathbb{R}^{N_2}:=\bigcup_{i\in[r], j\in[r']}S_{N_1,\varepsilon}^{[i]}\times {S'}_{N_2,\varepsilon}^{[j]} \cup T
$, where 
\begin{eqnarray}
S^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}&:=&\{z\in\mathbb{R}^{N_1}\,\:\, R_i\sqrt{N_1}\leq \|z\|_2\leq R_{i+1}\sqrt{N_1}\}\,,\nonumber\\
{S'}^{[i]}_{N_2,\varepsilon}&:=&\{z\in\mathbb{R}^{N_2}\,\:\, R'_i\sqrt{N_2}\leq \|z\|_2\leq R'_{i+1}\sqrt{N_2}\}\,,\nonumber\\
T&:=&\{z\in\mathbb{R}^{N_1}\,\:\, \|z\|_2\geq {N_1}^{\delta+\frac12}\}\cup \{z\in\mathbb{R}^{N_2}\,\:\, \|z\|_2\geq {N_2}^{\delta+\frac12}\}\,.\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}

Again $T$ can be neglected due to Lemma \ref{lemma:coda}. We have to evaluate
\begin{eqnarray}
&&Z^{\rho^2}_{N_1,N_2}[i,j]:=\int_{S^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}\times {S'}_{N_2,\varepsilon}^{[j]}}\rho^2_{N_1N_2}(dxdy)e^{-\beta H_{N_1,N_2}(x,y)}\,,\nonumber\\
&=&\frac{|S^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}\times {S'}_{N_2,\varepsilon}^{[j]}|}{\sqrt{2\pi\theta}^{N_1+N_2}} e^{-\frac{\tilde R^2_iN_1+{R'}^2_jN_2}{2\theta}-\sqrt{N_1N_2}r\left(\tilde{R}_i, \tilde{R'}_j\right)+\OOO{\varepsilon}} \int_{S^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}\times {S'}_{N_1,\varepsilon}^{[j]}}\sigma^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}(dx)\sigma^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}(dy) e^{-\beta H_{N_1,N_2}(x,y)}\,,\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
where the $\tilde R_i$ and $\tilde {R'}_i$ are introduced as before (see (\ref{eq:Rtilde})). Therefore

\begin{eqnarray}
A_{N_1,N_2,\beta}[i,j]&:=&\frac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log Z^{\rho^2}_{N_1,N_2,\beta}[i,j]\nonumber\\
&=&\frac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log\left(\frac{|S^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}\times {S'}_{N_2,\varepsilon}^{[j]}|}{\sqrt{2\pi\theta}^{N_1+N_2}}\right)+\frac{\OOO{\varepsilon}}{N_1+N_2} -\frac{\tilde R^2_i+{R'}^2_j}{2\theta}\nonumber\\
&-&\frac{\sqrt{N_1N_2}}{N_1+N_2}r\left(\tilde R_i, \tilde {R'}_j\right)+\widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}(\tilde R_i, \tilde R_j)\nonumber\,,
\end{eqnarray}
where $\widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}(\tilde R_i, \tilde {R'}_j)$ is the free energy of the RBM whose priors are the spherical shell measures of centres $\tilde R_i, \tilde {R'}_j$. The argument to pass to the thermodynamic limit is then the same, so (\ref{eq:mainRBM2}) is obtained.
nodes.statement_short: Slice both Gaussian layers into shells and repeat.

nodes.name: Shell slicing
nodes.statement:
We start by $i)$, where we deal with a single Gaussian prior. 
Let $\varepsilon>0$, $\delta>0$. From now on we will systematically omit the dependence on $\delta$ of the objects we will operate with. Let further $r<N_1^{\delta}/\varepsilon$, $R_0:=0$, $R_{r+1}:=N_1^{\delta}$, $\{R_i\}_{i=1,\ldots,r}\subset[0,N_1^{\delta})$ with $|R_{i+1}-R_i|<2\varepsilon$, and decompose
$
\mathbb{R}^{N_1}:=\bigcup_{i=0}^rS^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}\cup T
$, where 
$$
S^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}:=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^{N_1}\,\:\, R_i\sqrt{N_1}\leq \|z\|_2\leq R_{i+1}\sqrt{N_1}\}\,,\quad T:=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^{N_1}\,\:\, \|z\|_2\geq {N_1}^{\delta+\frac12}\}\,.
$$
Comparing with (\ref{eq:Sfshell}) one easily sees that the $S^{[i]}_{\varepsilon,N_1}$ are spherical shells. We denote by $\sigma^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}$ the uniform distributions on  these shells.
nodes.statement_short: Slice $\mathbb R^{N_1}$ into thin shells and a tail set $T$.

nodes.name: Decompose partition function
nodes.statement:
Then we have
\begin{equation} Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_1}=\sum_{i=0}^r Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2}[i]+\tilde Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2}\,,
\end{equation}
where
$$
Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2}[i]:=\int_{S^{[i]}_{N_1,\varepsilon}}\rho_{N_1}(dx)e^{-\beta H_{N_1,N_2}(x)}\,,\quad \tilde Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2}:=\int_{T}\rho_{N_1}(dx)e^{-\beta H_{N_1,N_2}(x)}\,.
$$
The tail term $\tilde Z^\rho_{N_1,N_2}$ gives a negligible contribution thanks to Lemma \ref{lemma:coda} and we will ignore it all the time.
nodes.statement_short: Split $Z^\rho$ over shells; the tail is negligible by Lemma 3.4.

nodes.name: Sandwich
nodes.statement:
Thus by (\ref{eq:dec}) we get 
$$
\max_{i\in[r]} Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2}[i]\leq Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2,\beta}\leq \frac{N^{\delta}}{\varepsilon}\max_{i\in[r]} Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2}[i]\,.
$$
Therefore setting
\begin{equation} A_{N_1,N_2}[i]:=\left(\frac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2}[i]\right)
\end{equation}
we have
\begin{equation} \max_{i\in[r]}\left(A_{N_1,N_2}[i]\right)\leq \frac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log Z^{\rho}_{N_1,N_2}\leq \max_{i\in[r]}\left(A_{N_1,N_2}[i]\right)+\frac{\delta\log N_1-\log \varepsilon}{N_1+N_2}\,. 
\end{equation}
So the free energy of $HM_{\rho}$ is given by the limit of $\max_{i\in[r]}\left(A_{N_1,N_2}[i]\right)$, provided it exists.
nodes.statement_short: Free energy equals the max over shells up to $o(1)$.

nodes.name: Shell free energy
nodes.statement_short: On each shell the Gaussian weight is constant up to $O(\varepsilon)$, giving spherical-shell free energies.

nodes.name: Limit and concavity
nodes.statement:
Thus we see that the existence of the thermodynamic limit is ensured by Lemma \ref{lemma-gusci} and we have

$$
\lim_{N_1,N_2}\max_{i\in[r]}\left(A_{N_1,N_2}[i]\right)=\sup_{R>0}\lim_{N_1,N_2}\left(\tilde A_{N_1,N_2,\varepsilon}(R)\right)=:\sup_{R>0}\tilde A_\varepsilon(R)\,. 
$$
By the uniform concavity of $\tilde A_\varepsilon(R)$ we have
$$
\lim_{\varepsilon\to0}\sup_{R>0}\tilde A_\varepsilon(R)=\sup_{R>0}\lim_{\varepsilon\to0}\tilde A_\varepsilon(R)=-\frac{\alpha}{2}\log\theta+\alpha\sup_{R>0}\left(\log R+\frac12+\alpha^{-1}A_{\sigma}(R,\beta)-r(R)-\frac{R^2}{2\theta}\right)\,
$$
and the proof of (\ref{eq:mainHM}) is concluded.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 2.3 and uniform concavity let $\varepsilon\to0$ pass inside the sup.
